rv.q: Those expecting a traditional take on Charles Dickens' classic holiday perennial may be in for a shock at the new Broadway version of 'A Christmas Carol.' Or at least they might be terribly perplexed by this dour production, whose additions only subtract from the potency of the transformative tale.
Dashiell Eaves is particularly memorable as the ever-optimistic Bob Cratchit, and the rest of the ensemble captivates with powerful, often musical, performances.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this Broadway adaptation, with praise for strong ensemble performances and inclusive casting of disabled actors as Tiny Tim, but criticism that the dour, non-traditional production undercuts the story's transformative power.

vs.sum: The Eugene O'Neill Theatre offers decent sightlines, though some seats may have minor obstructions due to the shallow rake. Sound quality is generally good, ensuring an enjoyable auditory experience. While the comfort level is typical for Broadway, with standard legroom and seat width, the theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant Georgian design. Facilities are adequate, with bars and merchandise available on both levels, though restroom capacity may be limited during peak times.

acc.note: No elevators. All accessible seating on Orchestra level. Infrared headsets and audio induction neck loops.
